content:
ashley: us-west1 burst: nodes showing metadata-flip storms during GPU scale-up. Attaches stuck, IO queues ballooning, lots of tiny writes. throwing in channel for quick triage.
riley: hit a few similar hosts earlier today?
ashley: not these exact hosts, different AZ. Pattern: cleaner consolidator started at 02:08z, then GPU batch launch at 02:12z. small write qdepth -> p99 writes 15-18ms.
jamie: paste dmesg excerpt and fio sample pls
ashley: dmesg snippet:
```
[    23.456789] blk_update_request: I/O error, dev nvme0n1, sector 12345678
[    23.457002] blk_update_request: I/O error, dev nvme0n1, sector 12345679
[    23.478901] EXT4-fs (nvme0n1p1): inode #98765: lost+found crosslink detected
```
ashley: fio quick read/write test from a good host vs affected host:
```
# good host
fio --name=seqwrite --bs=128k --size=1g --iodepth=16 -> bw 450MB/s lat 0.9ms
# affected
fio --name=seqwrite --bs=4k --size=1g --iodepth=16 -> bw 42MB/s lat 12.4ms
```
marc: That fio delta suggests lots of small-write amplification or scheduler thrash. Any kernel scheduler changes rolled out?
ashley: No kernel rollouts. Recent change: overlayfs metadata consolidation tweak deployed to ephemeral-population at 01:40z (overlay.merge_spread=true).
jamie: Could overlay consolidation plus janitor compact be creating metadata write storms? small metadata ops cause heavy write amplification on NVMe.
riley: Also seeing frequent fsync bursts in our attach path which synchronously writes metadata. If janitor compacts many small files you get many fsyncs.
devin: Two levers: 1) throttle janitor/compactor 2) switch affected hosts to write-back caching (if safe) or delayed fsync for ephemeral pools. Both have tradeoffs for data durability.
ops: Cost/risk callout: delaying fsync increases risk of losing transient ephemeral data on a crash; but these are temp files tied to jobs, acceptable for low-priority pools. We should classify pools.
jamie: Can we patch janitor to batch metadata commits? i.e., coalesce metadata flushes every 200ms rather than per-file.
marc: We tried a batching patch in staging months ago. It reduces IOps but increases peak write sizes. Works well if queue depth is limiting.
wanda: Quick mitigation: pause compactor on ephemeral-lowprio for 20m, enable metadata-flush batching on 10% canary, monitor attach backlog.
ashley: running pause: `infractl patch-janitor --region us-west1 --pool ephemeral-lowprio --pause 1200`
jamie: also enabling metadata batch flag: `infra-config set ephemeral.overlay.metadata_batch_ms=200 --hosts <canary>`
wanda: canary hosts showing immediate p99 improvement: 18ms -> 7.2ms within 90s. attach backlog down ~70%.
marc: Good. Any SMART or media errors?
ashley: SMART shows rising wear on a subset but no reallocated sectors. dmesg I/O errors look queuing related, not media.
jamie: propose next steps: 1) extend pause to full flagged set for 30m 2) roll metadata_batch to 30% if stable 3) create alert for "metadata_write_pattern" (high metadata fsync rate + avg write size <8KB)
ops: add note to cost model: if we defer compaction during scale-ups, we push more cleanup later -> slightly higher background IO overnight. Need numbers.
riley: also recommend adding a kernel-level scheduler test: try bfq on 5 hosts to compare p99. enqueue_depth tunables might help.
devin: I'll prep a quick bfq toggle script: `infractl set-io-scheduler --hosts <list> --scheduler bfq` and compare over 10m windows. rollback is simple.
oncall-bot: @oncall (jamie) acknowledged. Incident tracked.
jamie: action items logged: (A) wanda pause compactor across flagged hosts (in progress) (B) jamie extend metadata_batch rollout on canary (C) devin run bfq experiment (D) ops run overnight cost/latency sim for deferring compaction.
ashley: thanks all, will keep posting charts. adding followup: runbook entry for "metadata consolidation during GPU scaleups" and a safeguard to not run compactor windows overlapping scheduled GPU launches.
marc: Agreed. Also add wear_delta threshold to avoid noisy alerts.
wanda: scaling pause to all 18 flagged hosts now.
jamie: attaching quick chart: attach-backlog drops sharply after pause.
ashley: closing for now, attaches recovering. we'll keep compactor paused for 25m then resume gradually with batching.
